reviewMethod: Antigravity drafts separately reviewed against complete archived version bodies and source notes; source discrepancies retained explicitly.

headings.title: Restraint of trade or commerce prohibited
headings.reviewNote: Declares contracts, combinations, or conspiracies in restraint of trade or commerce unlawful.

headings.title: Monopolization and attempt to monopolize prohibited
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits monopolizing, attempting to monopolize, or conspiring to monopolize trade or commerce.

headings.title: Exclusive dealing and tying arrangements
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits exclusive dealing or tying leases, sales, or rebates on commodities that may substantially lessen competition or tend to create a monopoly (original-rolls footnote: 'persons').

entries.reviewSummary: Checked against archived full text, 1974 S.B. 424 history, and original-rolls footnote ('persons' in subsection 3); all 3 headings retained and footnote documented in subsection 3.

headings.title: Exemption for labor and agricultural organizations
headings.reviewNote: Exempts nonprofit labor, agricultural, or horticultural mutual-help organizations from antitrust laws.

headings.title: Exemption for regulated activities
headings.reviewNote: Exempts activities and arrangements expressly approved or regulated by state or federal regulatory bodies.

headings.title: Exemption for electric and water territorial agreements
headings.reviewNote: Exempts PSC-approved written electric territorial agreements under chapter 394 and PSC-approved written water territorial agreements under section 247.172.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked against archived full text and 1974-1991 history (effective 5-29-91); retained subsections 1-2 and broadened subsection 3 title/note to include PSC-approved water territorial agreements under section 247.172.

headings.title: Criminal penalty for antitrust violations
headings.reviewNote: Violating section 416.031(1) or (2) (original-rolls footnote: 'subsections') is a misdemeanor punishable by up to $50,000 fine and/or up to one year in county jail; bars AG prosecution during pending federal antitrust indictment or information on substantially same matter.

headings.title: Attorney general criminal prosecution authority
headings.reviewNote: Directs attorney general with county prosecutor assistance to investigate and prosecute criminal antitrust offenses.

headings.title: Civil penalty for court order contempt
headings.reviewNote: Imposes civil penalty up to $20,000 for contempt of a court order enforcing section 416.031 in an AG proceeding, with continuing circuit court jurisdiction.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked against archived full text, 1974 S.B. 424 history, and original-rolls footnote ('subsections'); all 3 headings retained, subsection 1 note updated for footnote/federal prosecution bar, and subsection 3 note corrected to remove ungrounded 'per day'.

headings.title: Circuit court jurisdiction
headings.reviewNote: Invests circuit courts with jurisdiction to prevent and restrain statutory antitrust violations.

headings.title: Attorney general enforcement duties
headings.reviewNote: Directs attorney general to institute civil enforcement actions and proceedings on behalf of state.

headings.title: Representation of political subdivisions and school districts
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes attorney general to represent municipalities, school districts, and political subdivisions in antitrust suits.

headings.title: Consent judgments and decrees
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes attorney general to enter into consent judgments or decrees subject to circuit court approval.

headings.title: Prima facie effect of state judgments
headings.reviewNote: Final state civil or criminal judgment is prima facie evidence against defendant in other parties' actions maintained within one year (original-rolls footnote: 'of'), excluding pre-testimony consent decrees and section 416.121 state actions.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked against archived full text, 1974 S.B. 424 history, and original-rolls footnote ('of' in subsection 5); all 5 headings retained and subsection 5 note updated.

headings.title: Preliminary and permanent injunctive relief
headings.reviewNote: Empowers circuit courts to grant preliminary and permanent injunctions and restraining orders against antitrust violations.

headings.title: Prohibitory injunctions and mandatory competitive relief
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes prohibitory injunctions to deter future violations and mandatory relief reasonably necessary to restore or preserve fair competition.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked against archived full text and 1974 S.B. 424 history; retained subsection 1 and replaced hallucinated divestiture/dissolution title in subsection 2 with prohibitory injunctions and mandatory competitive relief.

headings.title: Creation of Antitrust Revolving Fund
headings.reviewNote: Creates Antitrust Revolving Fund in state treasury for antitrust administration and enforcement.

headings.title: Appropriation and permissible uses
headings.reviewNote: Makes fund moneys available upon appropriation for attorney general investigation, enforcement, and expert expenses.

headings.title: Deposit of antitrust recoveries
headings.reviewNote: Directs deposit of ten percent of attorney general civil antitrust recoveries into revolving fund.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked against archived full text and 1974 S.B. 424 history; all 3 headings retained covering Antitrust Revolving Fund creation, permissible enforcement uses, and deposit of 10% of recoveries plus court costs.

headings.title: Civil investigative demand issuance
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes attorney general to issue civil investigative demand for documentary material prior to civil proceedings.

headings.title: Contents and requirements of demand
headings.reviewNote: Requires civil investigative demand to state antitrust conduct, describe documents, set return date, and identify custodian.

headings.title: Scope limitations on demand
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits unreasonable demands under subpoena standards and protects privileged materials from disclosure.

headings.title: Manner of service
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes service of civil investigative demand by delivery to business/residence (original-rolls footnote: 'persons') or by certified mail, return receipt requested.

headings.title: Proof of service
headings.reviewNote: Requires verified return or post office return receipt as proof of service of civil investigative demand.

headings.title: Designation of document custodian
headings.reviewNote: Directs attorney general to designate staff member as document custodian for produced materials.

headings.title: Compliance and document production
headings.reviewNote: Requires recipient to make documentary material available for inspection and copying at principal place of business.

headings.title: Custodian responsibilities and confidentiality
headings.reviewNote: Requires custodian to take physical custody and prohibits public disclosure without producer consent.

headings.title: Examination of material by state attorneys
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes custodian to deliver materials to designated state attorneys for court or grand jury use, with return of materials not entered into record (original-rolls footnote: 'has').

headings.title: Return of documents upon completion
headings.reviewNote: Directs custodian to return produced materials and copies not entered into court or grand jury record upon completion of investigation and proceedings (original-rolls footnote: 'has').

headings.title: Return of unused documents
headings.reviewNote: Requires return of produced documents if no case is instituted within reasonable time after investigation.

headings.title: Successor custodian appointment
headings.reviewNote: Directs AG to appoint successor custodian upon death, disability, separation, or relief, with written notice; successor assumes duties (original-rolls footnote: 'regards') without liability for prior defaults.

headings.title: Attorney general petition to enforce demand
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes AG to petition circuit court where person resides, is found, or transacts business (original-rolls footnote: 'persons') for enforcement order upon noncompliance or refusal to surrender material.

headings.title: Recipient petition to modify or set aside demand
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes served person (original-rolls footnote: 'persons') to petition circuit court within 20 days (or shorter return period) to modify or set aside demand, tolling compliance time during pendency.

headings.title: Producer petition to enforce custodian duties
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes document producer at any time during custody to petition circuit court where custodian's office is situated for order requiring custodian to perform statutory duties.

headings.title: Court jurisdiction, writ of prohibition, and contempt
headings.reviewNote: Grants circuit court jurisdiction to hear petitions and enter orders; final orders are appealable by writ of prohibition, and disobedience is punishable as contempt.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked against archived full text, 1974 S.B. 424 history, and all three original-rolls footnotes ('has', 'regards', 'persons'); corrected rotated/shifted headings in subsections 13-15, broadened subsection 16 (writ of prohibition), and fixed subsection 4 certified-mail note.

headings.title: Venue of civil and criminal antitrust actions
headings.reviewNote: Requires civil or criminal actions under sections 416.011 to 416.161 to be brought in circuit court where any defendant resides, engages in business, or has an agent, unless otherwise provided.

headings.title: Four-year statute of limitations and nonrevival
headings.reviewNote: Bars any action under sections 416.011 to 416.161 unless commenced within four years of accrual; does not revive causes barred on August 13, 1974.

headings.title: Tolling of limitations during state proceedings
headings.reviewNote: Tolls statute of limitations for private actions during pendency of state proceedings and for one year thereafter.

headings.title: Interstate commerce defense barred
headings.reviewNote: Bars defense that challenged anticompetitive conduct affects or involves interstate or foreign commerce.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked against archived full text and 1974 S.B. 424 history; replaced wrong/shifted headings in subsections 1-2 to reflect venue and general 4-year limitations/nonrevival, and retained subsections 3-4.

headings.title: Sale of milk products below cost prohibited
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits processors and distributors from advertising or selling milk products below cost to divert trade or destroy competition.

headings.title: Prima facie evidence of below-cost sale
headings.reviewNote: Establishes that proof of advertising or selling milk products below cost is prima facie evidence of violation.

headings.title: Prohibition on nonmilk cross-subsidization
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits using profits from nonmilk products to subsidize or lower cost calculations for milk products.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked against archived full text, 1959 H.B. 255 history, and 1962 Borden/1968 Dean Foods annotations; all 3 headings retained covering below-cost milk sales, prima facie evidence, and nonmilk cross-subsidy bar.

headings.title: Locality price discrimination in milk sales prohibited
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits processors and distributors from discriminating in milk product prices between towns, cities, or counties.

headings.title: Prima facie evidence of price discrimination
headings.reviewNote: Establishes proof of price differences between localities from same plant as prima facie evidence of violation.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked against archived full text, 1959 H.B. 255 history, and 1964 Foremost Dairies volume-pricing annotation; both headings retained covering locality price discrimination (with transportation exception) and prima facie evidence.

headings.title: Retail sales of milk below cost prohibited
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits nonprocessing retailers from advertising or selling milk products below invoice cost with anticompetitive intent.

headings.title: Prima facie evidence of retailer below-cost sale
headings.reviewNote: Archived text states proof of advertising, offer, or sale of milk products by a nonprocessing retailer is prima facie evidence of violation (omitting 'for less than cost' in text).

entries.reviewSummary: Checked against archived full text and 1959 H.B. 255 history; both headings retained and archived omission of 'for less than cost' in subsection 2 explicitly noted.

headings.title: Bulk milk sales below cost prohibited
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits bulk milk handlers from selling bulk milk below cost with anticompetitive intent or effect.

headings.title: Prima facie evidence of bulk milk below-cost sale
headings.reviewNote: Establishes proof of bulk milk sale below cost as prima facie evidence of violation.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked against archived full text and 1959 H.B. 255 history; both headings retained covering bulk milk handler below-cost sales and prima facie evidence.

headings.title: Combination sales below aggregate cost prohibited
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits selling milk products in combination with other items at price below aggregate individual costs.

headings.title: Prima facie evidence of unlawful combination sale
headings.reviewNote: Establishes proof of combined sale below aggregate prices as prima facie evidence of violation.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked against archived full text and 1959 H.B. 255 history; both headings retained covering below-aggregate combination milk sales and prima facie evidence.

headings.title: Rebates and discriminatory gifts by distributors prohibited
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits milk processors and distributors from giving gifts, loans, or discriminatory rebates to purchasers.

headings.title: Prima facie evidence of unlawful gift
headings.reviewNote: Establishes proof of giving or offering anything of value as prima facie evidence of violation.

headings.title: Receipt of prohibited rebates by purchasers prohibited
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits milk purchasers from accepting unlawful rebates, advertising allowances, or discriminatory services.

headings.title: Prima facie evidence of unlawful receipt
headings.reviewNote: Establishes proof of acceptance of value by milk purchaser as prima facie evidence of violation.

headings.title: Point-of-sale advertising exemption
headings.reviewNote: Exempts processor or distributor point-of-sale advertising materials provided to retailer without cost.

headings.title: Prompt payment discount exemption
headings.reviewNote: Exempts cash discounts of two percent or less for prompt payment on or before specified date.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked against archived full text, 1959 H.B. 255 history, and 1964/1982 annotations (Adams Dairy, Foremost Dairies [archived '(l964)' typo], Fleming Foods); all 6 headings retained.

headings.title: Subpoena authority and administration of oaths
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes director to issue subpoenas and administer oaths in milk marketing investigations.

headings.title: Contempt penalty for failure to obey court order
headings.reviewNote: Designates willful failure to obey judicial subpoena enforcement order as contempt of court.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked against archived full text and 1959 H.B. 255 history; both headings retained covering director subpoena/oath authority with court enforcement and contempt penalty.

headings.title: Complainant expense bond requirement
headings.reviewNote: Requires complainant to post one thousand dollar bond to defray investigation expenses upon filing complaint.

headings.title: Release of bond upon actionable violation
headings.reviewNote: Releases complainant bond liability when investigation reveals actionable violation resulting in litigation.

headings.title: Liability for expenses upon nonactionable complaint
headings.reviewNote: Requires complainant to defray actual investigation expenses up to one thousand dollars if complaint lacks merit.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked against archived full text and 1959 H.B. 255 history; all 3 headings retained covering $1,000 complainant bond, bond release upon violation, and complainant expense liability up to $1,000.

headings.title: License requirement for milk processors and distributors
headings.reviewNote: Requires milk manufacturing plants and distributors to obtain annual operating license from director.

headings.title: Annual license issuance and posting
headings.reviewNote: Requires license issuance on July first, conspicuous posting, and fee payment based on volume.

headings.title: License fee caps and annual rate setting
headings.reviewNote: Directs director to set annual license fees after hearing, subject to statutory hundredweight rate caps.

headings.title: Suspension and revocation of license
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes director to suspend or revoke distributor or processor license for statutory violations.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked against archived full text and 1959-1995 history notes; all 4 headings retained covering processor/distributor licensing (cottage cheese exempt), July 1 issuance/posting, fee caps, and suspension/revocation/section 536.024 rulemaking.

headings.title: Milk control fund creation
headings.reviewNote: Directs deposit of milk processor and distributor license fees into state treasury milk control fund.

headings.title: Appropriation requirement for fund disbursements
headings.reviewNote: Restricts fund disbursements to legislative appropriations for milk marketing law administration.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked against archived full text and 1959 H.B. 255 history; both headings retained covering Milk Control Fund creation and appropriation-only disbursements.

headings.title: Service of process on secretary of state
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes service of process on secretary of state for nonresident milk processors and distributors.

headings.title: Registered or certified mail forwarding to defendant
headings.reviewNote: Requires secretary of state to immediately forward notice of service, process, and petition to each defendant by restricted, registered, or certified mail.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked against archived full text and 1959 H.B. 255 history; retained subsection 1 and aligned subsection 2 title/note to include certified mail alongside restricted/registered mail.

headings.title: Sale of motor fuel below cost prohibited
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits selling or offering motor fuel below cost (416.605(2)) with intent to injure competition, induce other purchases, unfairly divert trade, or injure a competitor (1996 court annotation notes 1995 deletion of 'or effect' held unconstitutional).

headings.title: Price discrimination below prevailing local price
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits selling or offering motor fuel at a lower price than charged others at the same time and distribution level with intent to injure competition (see 1996 annotation on 'or effect').

headings.title: Predatory transfer pricing to affiliates
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits selling or transferring motor fuel to self or affiliate at a different marketing level below resale price charged others at same time/level with intent to injure competition (see 1996 annotation on 'or effect').

entries.reviewSummary: Checked against archived full text, 1993/1995 history, 1996 unconstitutionality annotation (Missouri Petroleum Marketers Assoc. invalidating 1995 H.B. 414 deletion of 'or effect'), and 2004 Quiktrip annotation; all 3 headings retained and notes aligned to archived 'intent' text with annotation caveats.

headings.title: Shipping, transportation, and quantity price differentials
headings.reviewNote: Exempts transfer or sale price differentials (including discounts, rebates, services, or facilities) at the same distribution level due to differences in shipping method, transportation, or quantity.

headings.title: Meeting competition defense for transfer and sale prices
headings.reviewNote: Exempts differences in transfer and sale prices or between sale prices at the same marketing level made in good faith to meet a competitor's equally low price.

headings.title: Meeting competition defense for retail sales below cost
headings.reviewNote: Exempts retail sales below cost resulting from good faith effort to meet competitor's equally low price.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked against archived full text and 1993 S.B. 374 history; fixed swapped headings/notes in subsections 1 and 2 (shipping/transportation/quantity differentials vs meeting-competition defense) and retained subsection 3.

headings.title: Civil penalty for below-cost motor fuel sales
headings.reviewNote: Imposes civil penalty from one thousand to five thousand dollars per violation, with each day constituting separate offense.

headings.title: Attorney general investigation and enforcement
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes attorney general and prosecuting attorneys to investigate violations and recover civil penalties.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked against archived full text and 1993 S.B. 374 history; both headings retained covering $1,000-$5,000 daily civil penalties and AG/prosecutor enforcement with general revenue deposit.

headings.title: Circuit court jurisdiction
headings.reviewNote: Vests circuit courts with jurisdiction to prevent and restrain motor fuel below-cost sales violations.

headings.title: Civil proceedings and special counsel
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes attorney general to institute civil injunction proceedings and employ special counsel.

headings.title: Consent judgments and decrees
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes attorney general to enter into consent judgments subject to court approval.

headings.title: Prima facie effect of state judgments
headings.reviewNote: Provides that final state judgment constitutes prima facie evidence in private motor fuel actions.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked against archived full text and 1993 S.B. 374 history; all 4 headings retained covering circuit court jurisdiction, AG civil proceedings/special counsel, consent judgments (31/60-day rules), and 1-year prima facie judgment effect.

headings.title: Bad faith patent infringement assertions prohibited
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits making bad faith assertions of patent infringement in demand letters.

headings.title: Factors evidencing bad faith demand
headings.reviewNote: Enumerates statutory factors court may consider as evidence of bad faith patent infringement assertion.

headings.title: Factors evidencing good faith demand
headings.reviewNote: Enumerates statutory factors court may consider as evidence that patent assertion was not made in bad faith.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked against archived full text and 2014 S.B. 706 history; all 3 headings retained covering bad-faith patent infringement demand letter bar, 7 bad-faith factors, and 7 good-faith factors.

headings.title: Attorney general investigation and enforcement authority
headings.reviewNote: Applies attorney general antitrust investigation and enforcement powers to bad faith patent assertions.

headings.title: Judicial remedies in attorney general actions
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes court to award any statutory relief in enforcement actions brought by attorney general.

headings.title: Deposit of recoveries in antitrust fund
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes deposit of attorney general recoveries into Antitrust Revolving Fund for operational expenses.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked against archived full text and 2014 S.B. 706 history; all 3 headings retained covering AG investigative/enforcement authority, available remedies, and Antitrust Revolving Fund deposits.

headings.title: Preservation of existing rights and remedies
headings.reviewNote: Preserves common law and statutory rights while barring unfair competition claims for compliant assertions.

headings.title: Exemption for statutory patent and biologics claims
headings.reviewNote: Exempts patent claims under 35 U.S.C. 271(e)(2) and 42 U.S.C. 262 from bad faith demand provisions.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked against archived full text and 2014 S.B. 706 history; both headings retained covering preservation of other remedies/good-faith patent notice safe harbor and exemption for 35 U.S.C. 271(e)(2) and 42 U.S.C. 262 claims.
